blocks.text: Setting up your estate inventory in Excel

Estate administration requires strict attention to detail. Start by creating a master inventory sheet. Columns should include Asset Name, Category, Valuation Date, Current Value, and Institution. Use Data Validation to create drop down lists for asset categories. This prevents typos and ensures your data remains clean. You can ask Lazur where to find the Data Validation menu if you get stuck.

Tracking debts is as important as tracking assets. Create a separate tab for liabilities. Include columns for Creditor Name, Claim Amount, Status, and Due Date. Use conditional formatting to highlight rows where the status is marked as Unpaid. This visual cue helps you prioritize payments and avoid late fees during the probate process.

You will often need to calculate totals across multiple assets. The SUMIFS function is your best friend here. It allows you to sum values based on multiple criteria, such as asset type and status. If you are comparing two columns to find discrepancies, use the VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP function to match data across sheets. These tools ensure your final accounting matches your bank statements perfectly.

Court filings require clean, readable documents. Hide gridlines to make your reports look like professional statements. Go to the View tab and uncheck Gridlines. Ensure your date formats are consistent. Use the Format Cells dialog to set dates to a standard format like DD/MM/YYYY. This keeps your records uniform and professional.

If you find yourself repeating the same steps, record a macro. A macro automates repetitive tasks like clearing a template or formatting a report. Just go to the Developer tab and click Record Macro. Perform the steps once, and Excel remembers them for next time.

Estate data is highly sensitive. Always protect your workbook with a password. Go to File > Protect Workbook and choose Encrypt with Password. Store this password in a secure password manager. Never leave sensitive estate files on an unprotected device.

faq.question: Can I use Excel on Mac for probate accounting?
faq.answer: Yes, Excel is a standard tool for tracking estate inventories, liabilities, and distributions. It provides the flexibility needed for custom estate reports.

faq.question: How do I speed up my work in Excel?
faq.answer: Mastering keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + T for tables and ⌘ + D for filling data will significantly reduce your time spent on manual entry.
